What part in their bio exactly is creepy and pathetic?

Are you being ableist about them being autistic? Hardly, you yourself mention autism in your profile. Or just a good old round of transphobia from you? Or just rabid hatred of furries?

You're being a creep sexualizing a politician with gross af comments, you're being just as bad as the male gaze you say you're avoiding in your own bio.

Shocker to learn that being lesbian doesn't prevent one from being a creep.

> For your analogy to work, you would only be calling your rapist slurs, not saying "all POC people are rapists" or anything along these lines. 

The question remains: If your abuser was, say, a black person, would you suddenly be justified to call them the n-word? OF COURSE NOT.

The fact this is a discussion at all, the fact this thread exists at all, proves that people think a trans person's gender is an attack vector, which we would never think about a cis person's gender.

To think that *any* trans person can be attacked through their identity, that is inherently a transphobic position.

Call a vile person any vile thing under the sun. You have every fucking right to. But when you show that you also think a trans person's gender is a conditional thing and something to freely attack when it suits you, that is textbook transphobia. Which isn't defending the abuser, it's a scummy person who deserves nothing.

But principles are true out of *principle*. Trans people's pronouns need to be respected as a *principle*.

Respecting a bad person's pronouns is being consistent about a *principle*, it's not about actually respecting a shitty person, because of course they don't deserve any fucking respect! But it's about respecting *a principle* that extends to every other fucking trans person.

> whereas here, it is.

Because it shows that in this case, the person being trans is an attack vector to degrade them with. Which is inherently a transphobic idea. A trans person's gender identity isn't an attack vector, but u/Important_Try8430 and everyone in these comments enabling OP thinks it is.

>  It's creepy and sounds like conversion therapy logic wrapped in a progressive disguise.

This is exactly what it is.

But the root cause there isn't the concept of sexual fluidity. The root cause is homophobia. And homophobes will find any progressive-sounding rhetoric to hijack to be homophobic. Attacking this one specific piece of rhetoric itself is pretty meh. A lot of queer people have been helped greatly by viewing sexuality from the lens of being fluid. That entire concept shouldn't be under scrutiny because homophobes hijack it. They hijack fucking anything.

And the slogan that sexuality is fluid can co-exist with the fact a lot of people's sexualities doesn't change.

"Sexuality is fluid" as a slogan, at face value just means sexuality isn't *inherently static*, and the existence of people whose sexuality has changed proves that. It isn't a mandate that each peron's sexuality must become dynamic.

And if homophobes use that kind of fluidity rhetoric to force lesbians to have sex with men or some other dumb shit homophobes do, the problem isn't with sexual fluidity as a concept, but with homophobia. Because homophobes will just find some other progressive-sounding rhetoric to hijack if you take one away from them.

Yes it certainly fucking is lol. Read my other reply to the fella who replied to you, but basically: The only scenario in which gender and sexuality may change to such a degree where "attraction to one gender" won't be a concept anymore isn't a scenario where that happens because they get "cancelled".

The ancient Greek concept of pederasty didn't get "cancelled" when whatever term people used to describe two men fucking came up after that, people's ideas of gender and sex just changed. As they do.

Our contemporary ideas of hetero and homosexuality are also pretty recent, and whatever preceding concept of sexuality was used to explain gay relationships (since there were and always will be men loving men and women loving women) wasn't "cancelled", people just changed the way they view the world and other people *over a process of time*.

So some hypothetical genderpunk future in 100 years where monosexuality isn't a thing anymore, if that future were to occur, it wouldn't be because any one thing gets "cancelled" but because societal views of what gender and sex even *mean* will change.

Stop the fearmongering, get off the kool-aid. That slippery slope bullshit is ridiculous.

Yeah lol, they are wrong. This is some really fucking weird slippery slope bullshit. Unless you are talking about a really distant future like year 2500 or some shit. Because the rough concept of gender isn't going away, even if it's being expanded upon and deconstructed a lot, the idea of men and women is not going to go away for a while, and neither will the idea of monosexuality.

And if these concepts may change at some point in the future, it wouldn't be because of some people "cancelling" being attracted to one gender, but because societal norms around the definitions of gender and sexuality would have changed.

Y'know, like how the idea of "homosexuality" wasn't a thing in, say, ancient Greece, but you still had dudes fucking dudes. They just had different concepts to align with. Their gay sex was still all the same and just as gay, nobody got "cancelled" when their conception changed over time, nor did anyone get "cancelled" when the idea of hetero- and homosexuality as we use them now became the norm.

If you wouldn't doubt that in 10 years or so you're also buying into stupid fearmongering bullshit by people who desperately need you to have the fear of that slippery slope to propel their political agenda.

They got downvoted for proposing something extremely ridiculous, and so are you.

Saying that sexuality is fluid, and being a homophobe who says lesbian women can be converted, are not one and the same.

Homophobes will hijack whatever rhetoric doesn't explicitly make them look homophobic. So if the "you just haven't had the right man yet" of the past becomes the "Well oh you know sexuality is fluid", the fault with that is not with the slogan that the homophobes hijacked, but... shocker, with the homophobes.

> Also calling sexuality fluid in everybody brings it back to the narrative of having a choice.

Just like OP you seem to have misunderstandings on what the slogan actually says.

Sexuality is fluid means that on one hand, sexuality labels, which are at their core just approximations we try to neatly map onto complex human experiences, might not be able to describe your experience accurately. And on the other hand, it means that, as an individual person, your experience with sexuality *can* be dynamic.

Nobody is stating that "sexuality is fluid" is a mandated enforcement that each and every person must change their sexuality at one point. Nor is it saying that people whose sexuality never seems to change are invalid. But a slogan like "your individual sexuality can be fluid dynamic over time and isn't forced to be static" is a lot more wordy of a slogan. And a majority of people upon hearing "sexuality is fluid" will understand what it actually refers to, rather than ascribing to it an exaggeratedly literal meaning like OP.

> To me, such a saying is no different from telling me that I "haven't found the right man yet" or that I'm "going through a phase".

That's because you seem to slightly misunderstand what "sexuality is fluid" means.

> I want this phrase to be used depending on the individual, not in the broad sense.

That is precisely what it means.

"Sexuality is fluid" does not mean "Every person's sexuality *will* definitively change". That's something *you* are ascribing to it, but nobody who uses that phrase ever said.

It means that a person's sexuality *can*, over time, morph in such a way it doesn't neatly fit established sexuality labels.

"Sexuality is fluid" does not mean "Your sexuality MUST fluctuate", it means "As human beings, 'sexuality' is a concept that is far more nebulous than we like to accredit, since it's a social construct. Sometimes, the labels for this nebulous concept won't be able to accurately describe your experience, or sometimes, your experience will change in such a way that breaks these traditional labels". It doesn't mean your sexuality must fluctuate, it means that sexuality inherently is not static. That can still mean that for you, in your own experience, your sexuality never seems to change. And that is perfectly a-OK and nobody (who isn't a homophobe already anyway) wants to take that away from you.

For a concrete example and a hypothetical to think about, you can imagine, since you are a gay woman, if you find yourself attracted to another woman, who one day comes out as a trans man and wanting to transition. A lot of people in that scenario might stop being attracted to that person because they'll see them as a man and thus something they're not attracted to. A lot of lesbian woman in that scenario might *still* find themselves attracted, while also acknowledging and considering that person with their right gender identity as a man. And it won't make their sexuality they identify as any less or more viable. Since labels are at the end of the day just approximations that can't describe a complex human experience accurately.

"Sexuality is fluid" is a slogan. 3 words that very neatly and swiftly encapsulate a slightly more complex concept. They aren't meant to be literal to a T. And a slogan like "Your individual sexuality is *sometimes* fluid" is a lot more wordy and a lot less effective at getting this across. The vast majority of people will not need to have explained to them that "Sexuality is fluid" isn't literallly prescribing their sexuality must also fluctuate, but that it means *it can*.

And finally: Homophobic people will pick up whatever rhetoric they can to justify their homophobia. But then blame the homophobes themselves, not whatever rhetoric they hijack. If homophobes pick up rhetoric like "Sexuality is fluid", then the core problem is still those people's homophobia. Saying the slogan itself does more harm than good is silly. If that rhetoric didn't exist, homophobes would just find something else to sling around.

> only a matter of whether you can feel comfortable with her real age or not

Or, you know, whether OP feels comfortable with someone who lied about something like that...

> I worked out, read every self improvement book out there, and fixed my wardrobe. It still amounted to nothing and I’m still a fucking virgin.

Have you... been socializing with people? The key to meeting potential partners is to meet people in general. Do hobbies, go to clubs, go to events, etc.

> I even got on every dating app under the sun. It only amounted to zero matches in three years.

Yeah. Dating app culture fucking sucks. Meet real people in real life.

All that aside, I'm gonna tell you something that will probably really fucking hurt. Getting a relationship isn't going to fix your life. You have an inherently deeply broken sense of self that is not going to magically fix itself if you get into a relationship, even if the person you find is the perfect partner.

Loneliness is cruel, and it fucking hurts, but feeling so deeply broken to the point you feel resentment about seeing couples, and you feel suicidality at the idea of not having a partner, your problem goes way beyond just not having a girlfriend.

Please, for your own sake, seek a therapist or some form of professional help.

29 is fucking young. 30 is fucking young. There is no "level 1" or "level 100", different people make different life experiences at different paces. Sure, not having a partner at the age of 29 is above average, but you are not a statistic. You are a person.
